Hi Daniel — great to hear from you, and glad the demo landed well.

I've attached Redwood's current DPA template (Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.2.pdf). A few notes up front to make the review efficient:

- Subprocessors: our primary hosting and inference infra are run on cloud providers (AWS and GCP) — we operate in region-specific projects and use a narrow set of managed services. We also leverage a backup/replication partner (Azure Blob Storage in EU regions for customers who require it). I'll attach a canonical subprocessor list in the next message (we maintain a published list and an attestation process).
- Transfers: for EU processing we rely on SCCs where appropriate; we support EU-hosted deployments and offer private VPC options to avoid cross-border transfers. For hosted customers opting into Redwood's hosted API, we can document the transfer mechanisms in the DPA (SCCs + documented safeguards).
- eSign: our standard execution path is DocuSign, but we can do AdobeSign on a per-deal basis. If Equinox prefers AdobeSign, that's fine — just confirm and we'll route through the correct workflow.

Questions for you (helps speed redlines):
1) Do you expect Equinox to request changes to the data retention/return clauses?
2) Are there any specific EU data residency requirements we should note (e.g., all copies must remain in EU region)?
3) Is your procurement team set on a wet-ink original for countersignature, or will an AdobeSign/DocuSign certificate suffice?

I'll copy Marissa (legal) and Karthik (AE) to loop in on any redline guidance and to confirm the subprocessor attestation path.

Thanks — attaching the DPA now.

Best,
Irene Choi
